3586.heading: SignalR Hub
3586.content:
A SignalR hub is the server-side endpoint through which clients and the application exchange named real-time messages. ASP.NET Core maps the hub to a route and makes its client communication interface available through dependency injection.

Application code can use the hub context to publish after a successful state change. Keeping the database write authoritative prevents a notification from claiming that an operation succeeded before it actually did.

In the chat project, a hub subclass exposes methods whose calls end in `Clients.All.SendAsync`, causing every connected client to invoke a named handler with the supplied values. The hub route is mapped during application startup after SignalR and the Azure SignalR integration are registered.

The callback converts the received payload into a state update that React can render. Cross-origin configuration must permit the connection when the client and API run at different origins.

3601.heading: Signal Time-of-Flight Ranging
3601.content: Signal time-of-flight ranging estimates distance by multiplying propagation time by the speed of the signal. In GPS, a receiver compares a satellite's coded timestamp with a locally generated replica and interprets their offset as travel time. Because receiver time is not initially synchronized to the satellite clocks, the raw result is a pseudorange containing a common clock-bias term as well as atmospheric and other errors.

3604.heading: Sigmoid Activation Function
3604.content:
The sigmoid activation function is a smooth S-shaped function whose output ranges from zero to one. Large negative inputs approach zero, large positive inputs approach one, and an input of zero produces one-half.

It supplies a differentiable approximation to a binary step while keeping activation bounded. Compared with the [[Tanh Activation Function]], sigmoid is not centered around zero because it does not produce negative outputs.

Its value depends on how optional it truly is. When a side quest contains narrative information needed to understand the main plot, players may experience it as required even if the system allows them to pass it by.

3616.title: Shutter Speed
3616.heading: Shutter Speed
3616.content:
Shutter speed is the duration for which a camera gathers light during an exposure. A longer duration records more light but also integrates movement over more time; a shorter duration reduces motion blur but admits less light.

The visible sharpness of moving objects can therefore be checked against the exposure time stored in metadata. The inference depends on the unknown speed and direction of motion and on camera movement, so it supplies a constraint rather than a unique reconstruction.

3619.content:
The shortest path problem asks for the route between graph vertices with the smallest [[Graph Path Length]]. In an unweighted graph this can mean the fewest edges; in a [[Weighted Graph]] it means the smallest sum of edge weights.

Enumerating every possible route is correct but can become infeasible. [[Dijkstra's Algorithm]] finds shortest paths from one starting vertex efficiently when edge weights are nonnegative.

3622.heading: Short Exact Sequence
3622.content:
A short exact sequence has the form 0 → A → B → C → 0. The first map is injective, its image is the kernel of the second map, and the second map is surjective.

It identifies A with a submodule of B and C with the corresponding quotient. If the sequence splits, then B is isomorphic to the direct sum A ⊕ C.

A short exact sequence of complexes 0 → C′ → C → C″ → 0 is exact at every degree and its maps commute with the differentials. Each component sequence 0 → C′ₙ → Cₙ → C″ₙ → 0 is short exact.

The interaction between componentwise exactness and the differentials creates connecting maps, producing a [[Long Exact Sequence in Homology]].

3631.heading: Shifted Inverse Power Method
3631.content:
The shifted inverse power method applies inverse iteration to $A-qI$. Its dominant reciprocal corresponds to the eigenvalue of $A$ nearest the chosen shift $q$.

Each step solves $(A-qI)y=x$ and normalizes the result. A good shift targets an interior eigenvalue much more directly than the ordinary [[Power Method]].

3634.title: Sheaf
3634.heading: Sheaf
3634.content:
A sheaf is a [[Presheaf]] whose sections are determined locally and whose compatible local sections glue uniquely to a section on their union. It turns local algebraic data into coherent global data.

The [[Structure Sheaf]] on a spectrum assigns localized rings to basic open sets. A [[Quasi-Coherent Sheaf]] similarly arises from localizing a module.

3637.title: Sheaf Stalk
3637.heading: Sheaf Stalk
3637.content:
The stalk of a [[Sheaf]] at a point collects sections defined on neighborhoods of that point, identifying two sections when they agree on some smaller neighborhood. It records only the local behavior near the point.

For the [[Structure Sheaf]] of Spec(A), the stalk at a prime p is the local ring A_p. Stalks therefore connect sheaf-theoretic locality with [[Localization at a Prime Ideal]].

The physical setting supplies a natural reference for speech, gaze, and gesture. Consistent registration and synchronized object state let actions appear to occur in one space rather than in disconnected private displays.

3643.heading: Shared Product Vision
3643.content:
A shared product vision is a clear, compelling, and stable understanding of what a team is making, what it will deliver, and how each person's work contributes. It turns a creative direction into coordinated action.

The vision should be documented, understood, and supported across the team without becoming immune to evidence. Necessary changes involve relevant stakeholders and are communicated deliberately so the project does not drift through accumulated local decisions.

Release planning can revisit the vision through a concise elevator statement, game-box exercise, positioning map, or ambitious release goal. The representation matters less than giving developers enough shared context to make aligned daily decisions while features emerge.

3652.content:
Shared pointers represent objects whose lifetime is jointly required by several clustering structures. A schema can be shared by all records in a dataset, and records or nodes can be referenced by clusters, results, and algorithms without manual reference counting.

Shared ownership simplifies lifetime management across polymorphic containers, but it does not automatically define who may mutate the object. Cycles among parent and child pointers also require care because reference counting alone cannot reclaim a closed ownership loop.

3655.title: Shared Authorship
3655.heading: Shared Authorship
3655.content:
Shared authorship occurs when players extend, rearrange, or create material within a game rather than only consuming what its original creators supplied. Level editors, scenario tools, role-playing facilitation, and modding can turn players into designers.

The original game still provides rules, examples, and a world that shape the new work. Sharing authorship therefore creates a continuing conversation between the initial design and what players imagine and build from it.

3658.title: Shared Accountability
3658.heading: Shared Accountability
3658.content:
Shared accountability means a team owns its collective result rather than treating each specialty as responsible only for local tasks. Members surface impediments, help where they can, and judge progress by integrated value.

Individual expertise and responsibility still matter, but they operate inside a common goal. This reduces the tendency to declare one component done while the product remains unusable.

3661.title: Shape Function
3661.heading: Shape Function
3661.content:
A shape function interpolates a field inside an element from its nodal values. Linear, quadratic, and higher-order polynomials provide progressively richer variation while remaining tied to the element's degrees of freedom.

Useful shape functions equal one at their own node and zero at the other nodes. This interpolation makes nodal unknowns the coefficients of the approximate field and supplies the derivatives used to calculate gradients, strain, or flux.

3664.title: Shadow IT
3664.heading: Shadow IT
3664.content:
Shadow IT is technology acquired or operated by a business unit without the knowledge or standard management of the organization's IT function. It often arises when official delivery is too slow or restrictive for an immediate business need.

Easy cloud purchasing lowers the threshold for creating shadow services. The resulting agility can carry untracked security, support, integration, duplication, and continuity risks, so governance should address the unmet demand that caused it rather than only prohibit the service.

3667.title: Shape Context
3667.heading: Shape Context
3667.content:
Shape context represents a point on an object boundary by a histogram of the relative locations of other boundary points. Log-polar bins preserve coarse information about both distance and direction.

Comparing these local histograms supports point correspondence and overall shape matching. The descriptor gains tolerance to small deformations through binning, while normalization can address scale and other geometric variation.

3685.title: Set
3685.heading: Set
3685.content:
A set is a collection whose membership is well defined. Sets may be described by listing elements or by a property that determines membership, and two sets are equal exactly when they contain the same elements.

Modern algebra uses sets as the underlying carriers for operations, relations, functions, groups, rings, and fields.

Order and repetition in a written list do not change the set it denotes. Membership is expressed by ∈, while the empty set is the unique set with no elements.

3688.content:
Set-based design begins with several feasible alternatives and narrows them as evidence accumulates. Design, art, and technology explore overlapping possibility sets, eliminating options that fail shared constraints while delaying commitment to one solution.

The apparent duplication buys protection against committing early to a path that later proves infeasible. Small parallel experiments are most valuable where uncertainty and the cost of late reversal are high.

3694.title: Set Difference
3694.heading: Set Difference
3694.content:
The set difference A ∖ B contains the elements that belong to A but not to B. In predicate form, A ∖ B = {x | x ∈ A ∧ x ∉ B}.

Unlike [[Union of Sets]] and [[Intersection of Sets]], set difference is not commutative: removing B's elements from A generally produces a different set from removing A's elements from B.

3697.title: Set Equality
3697.heading: Set Equality
3697.content:
Set equality means two sets have exactly the same elements. A standard proof establishes both inclusions: every element of the first set lies in the second, and conversely.

This two-direction method recurs when proving equality of cosets, generated structures, fields, and ideals.

In predicate notation, A = B means that x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ B for every x. This is equivalent to proving both A ⊆ B and B ⊆ A.

3700.content:
The session layer of the OSI model manages the continuing conversation between two applications. It establishes, coordinates, and ends a session and describes whether communication can proceed in simplex, half-duplex, or full-duplex form.

A session is a logical interaction above raw delivery. Its state must define which side may transmit, how an interrupted conversation resumes, and when the exchange is complete.

Service-based pricing derives the charge from the benefit or commitment delivered to the consumer rather than only the provider's underlying resource consumption. Scope, service levels, transferred delivery risk, and money saved can therefore influence the amount.

The book groups fixed, volume, and tiered approaches in this category. The model is strongest when both parties can define the service boundary and measure the unit on which the charge depends.

3706.title: Session Authentication
3706.heading: Session Authentication
3706.content:
Session authentication keeps an authenticated user's state associated with a server-managed session and sends a session identifier with later requests. The server uses that identifier to recover the corresponding login state.

This is stateful because the server must retain session information. [[Token-Based Authentication]] instead gives the client a signed token that carries information used to validate subsequent requests.

3709.title: Service Worker
3709.heading: Service Worker
3709.content:
A service worker is a script the browser runs in the background without its own user interface. It can intercept fetch events, manage cached resources, and support application startup when the network is unavailable.

Because it mediates network resources, registration requires a [[Secure Origin]]. Its cache rules must distinguish application files from requests that should always reach the server.

A service level objective is a measurable target used to judge one characteristic of a service. Examples include uptime, throughput, available capacity, response time, recovery time, or delivery time.

An SLA should express outcomes that matter to the consumer rather than exposing every internal infrastructure metric. More specific [[Service Level Objective]]s give the provider measurable targets that support the overall agreement.

3730.title: Service Autonomy
3730.heading: Service Autonomy
3730.content:
Service autonomy means a service owns its execution and can remain operational without synchronously depending on another service for every action. Inputs may arrive from outside, but their temporary absence should leave the service idle rather than unable to start.

The order worker receives sales orders through an [[Azure Storage Queue]], so the producer and consumer do not need to be available simultaneously. This loose timing relationship is what allows several worker replicas to process the same backlog.

3733.title: Serverless Computing
3733.heading: Serverless Computing
3733.content:
Serverless computing runs application functions on provider-managed infrastructure whose servers, allocation, and scaling are hidden from the developer's normal workflow. It does not mean no hardware exists; it means the application does not provision or maintain that hardware directly.

The Azure Functions model in the book scales small stateless operations according to demand and charges in relation to use. This reduces infrastructure work, while the function still needs explicit inputs, outputs, configuration, and failure handling.

3742.title: Server-Side Paging
3742.heading: Server-Side Paging
3742.content:
Server-side paging applies a page index and page size to a query before the result crosses the API boundary. The response returns only the requested records together with enough metadata, such as a total count, for the client to render navigation.

It reduces database materialization, network transfer, and browser rendering for large datasets. Page changes require new [[HTTP Request|requests]], so sorting and filtering parameters must be sent with the page selection.

For a high-demand API, paging also bounds the work performed by any one collection request. The page size remains a capacity choice: a value that is too large loses the protection, while one that is too small creates excess navigation and request traffic.

Server-side Blazor runs component C# code on the server and transmits interface updates to the browser through SignalR. It uses the Blazor component model without running that application code as WebAssembly on the client.

The source identifies server-side Blazor as the flavor released with .NET Core 3. Its architecture trades the client's runtime download for a continuing real-time connection to server-hosted state and execution.

3751.title: Server Push
3751.heading: Server Push
3751.content:
Server push is the delivery of a message from the server to a client without a new client-initiated request for that message. SignalR uses this pattern to notify connected React applications after relevant server events.

Push reduces the delay and repeated traffic of polling, but the message is still a notification within a fallible connection. The client must update state deliberately and recover its authoritative view when necessary.

3754.title: Server Virtualization
3754.heading: Server Virtualization
3754.content:
Server virtualization allows one physical host to run several independent [[Virtual Machine]]s. Each virtual machine can have its own operating system and applications even though the instances share the host's processors, memory, storage, and networking hardware.

Consolidation can reduce procurement, floor-space, cooling, electricity, and maintenance requirements. In cloud computing, virtualization also makes pooled instances easier to activate and release, but billing, self-service, service catalogs, and orchestration are additional systems layered around it.

3757.title: Servant Leadership
3757.heading: Servant Leadership
3757.content:
Servant leadership treats the growth and effectiveness of people and the whole system as the leader's primary responsibility. It emphasizes listening, care, foresight, community, systems thinking, and removing conditions that prevent good work.

Serving does not mean avoiding standards. A servant leader expects capable people to pursue ambitious results, permits responsible mistakes, and creates the trust needed for honest learning.

No single formulation supports every cell type as effectively as serum, and purified growth factors can make defined media expensive at manufacturing scale.

3763.title: Serious Game
3763.heading: Serious Game
3763.content:
A serious game is designed to address a real-world purpose through play, such as education, training, public communication, or problem solving. Entertainment can support the purpose even when it is not the final objective.

The real-world goal does not excuse weak game design. Players still need intelligible rules, meaningful challenges, useful feedback, and reasons to remain engaged.

3766.heading: Sequential Pattern Feature Mining
3766.content:
Sequential pattern feature mining discovers ordered symbol patterns and converts their occurrence into classifier inputs. Class-sensitive criteria favor subsequences that distinguish labels rather than merely appearing frequently overall.

The candidate space grows combinatorially as patterns lengthen. Minimum support, upper bounds, closed-pattern constraints, and wrapper evaluation reduce the search while preserving features likely to improve classification.

A complete pattern-defined feature also specifies how matches become values, such as binary presence, cumulative frequency, positional indicators, or windowed counts. Mining and mapping are therefore distinct design decisions.

The palette should also preserve legibility against boundaries and backgrounds rather than using hue changes that introduce false categories.

3772.title: Sequential and Simultaneous Multiphysics Solutions
3772.heading: Sequential and Simultaneous Multiphysics Solutions
3772.content:
In a sequential multiphysics solution, one physics is solved first and its field is passed as input to another. This can reduce the size of each solve and is appropriate when feedback from the later physics to the earlier one is negligible.

A simultaneous solution assembles interdependent fields so they converge together. It is needed when fluid motion changes temperature and temperature also changes the flow, as in [[Nonisothermal Flow|nonisothermal systems]], but the tighter coupling can demand better initial states and solver control.

Sequential tasks finish one unit of work before starting the next, preserving an obvious order and simple access to shared state. Concurrent tasks make progress during overlapping periods and can improve throughput or responsiveness when their work is independent.

Concurrency is useful only when the workload and dependencies permit it. Coordination, scheduling, and contention add costs, so independent operations should be identified explicitly and performance should be measured rather than inferred from the number of tasks.

3778.title: Sequence
3778.heading: Sequence
3778.content:
A sequence is an ordered list of values whose members are called terms. Each term is associated with a position, usually a [[Natural Number]], so the same value appearing at different positions still counts as a different occurrence.

A [[Law of Formation]] describes the ordering. It may specify a constant additive change, producing an [[Arithmetic Progression]], or a constant multiplicative change, producing a [[Geometric Progression]]. A formula for the (n)th term permits a distant position to be evaluated without constructing every earlier term.

3781.title: Sequence-Constrained Hierarchical Clustering
3781.heading: Sequence-Constrained Hierarchical Clustering
3781.content:
Sequence-constrained clustering permits a merge only between adjacent segments of an ordered series. In the book's screenplay and tweet analyses, scene or message chronology is preserved while complete-link agglomeration builds a nested hierarchy.

The resulting dendrogram can expose where consecutive passages cease to resemble one another. Without the sequence constraint, a conventional clusterer might put distant but similar scenes together and erase the narrative position of a transition. The constraint changes what the tree means, not merely how it is drawn.

3784.content:
Sequence data representation preserves the order of elements in objects such as event logs, biological sequences, or symbol strings. Derived variables can encode which patterns occur, where they occur, and how often they recur.

Unlike an unordered item set, a sequence distinguishes arrangements containing the same elements. Feature design must therefore specify both a pattern and the rule used to map its matches into numerical values.

3787.title: Sequence Recognition
3787.heading: Sequence Recognition
3787.content:
Sequence recognition infers hidden labels, states, or models from an ordered series of observations. The temporal decomposition represents how earlier hidden states constrain later ones and how each state produces evidence.

Order provides information that isolated classification discards. Filtering supports online recognition, while smoothing can reinterpret earlier elements after later observations become available.

Separation of privilege requires more than one independent condition before granting a sensitive capability. Examples include two-person approval or authentication that combines distinct evidence.

The principle reduces the chance that one stolen credential, compromised component, or mistaken decision can authorize a critical action. Its cost is additional coordination and recovery complexity.

Separation of concerns assigns different responsibilities to different parts of a system so each can change without carrying unrelated duties. A full-stack application separates persistence entities, API output, client communication, and presentation even when their data initially looks similar.

An [[Entity Framework Core Entity]] should model stored state, while a [[Data Transfer Object]] exposes the controlled shape needed by the client. An [[Angular Service]] handles reusable communication so an [[Angular Component]] can focus on interface state.

3796.content:
A sequence control structure executes a series of steps one after another in a specified order. The output or changed state produced by one step is then available to the steps that follow it.

Sequence is the simplest [[Control Structure]], but order still matters. Reversing two operations may change the result, especially when later work depends on values calculated or data transformed earlier in an [[Algorithm]].

3799.title: Separable Programming
3799.heading: Separable Programming
3799.content:
Separable programming approximates a nonlinear problem whose objective and constraints can be written as sums of single-variable functions.

Each nonlinear function is replaced by a piecewise-linear approximation over selected breakpoints. The resulting model can be handled as a [[Linear Programming]] problem, with approximation quality depending on the breakpoint spacing.

A sentient tissue model is a hypothetical or future construct complex enough to have subjective experiences such as pain. A sensory neuron can detect a damaging stimulus without proving conscious experience, while integration with sufficiently complex neural processing raises a harder question.

Researchers can reduce uncertainty by limiting unnecessary neural complexity and defining review thresholds before such capabilities are demonstrated.

3805.title: Sentence Planner
3805.heading: Sentence Planner
3805.content:
A sentence planner selects and organizes the information that a generated response should communicate. It can decide which facts matter, their order, and whether several facts should be combined or summarized.

The plan sits between the [[Dialog Manager]]'s symbolic action and surface realization. A [[Microplanner]] then chooses more detailed structures for expressing the selected content.

3808.heading: Sensory Layer of Play
3808.content:
The sensory layer is the player's immediate perception of a game through image, sound, touch, movement, and other bodily channels. It determines which signals are available before the player interprets what those signals mean.

Design at this layer directs [[Attention]] through contrast, rhythm, motion, volume, texture, and timing. A crucial state change that cannot be perceived cannot reliably support the higher informational and interactive layers.

3814.heading: Sensor Noise
3814.content:
Sensor noise is the variation added when a camera converts light into digital measurements. It includes changing random components as well as stable differences in how individual sensor elements respond to the same illumination.

Forensic analysis uses both properties. Random-noise level should vary plausibly with brightness and camera processing, while the stable component can identify a device. Denoising, sharpening, compression, resizing, saturation, and low exposure all alter the observable signal.

3817.title: Sensor Fusion
3817.heading: Sensor Fusion
3817.content:
Sensor fusion combines measurements from multiple sensors to obtain tracking behavior that no single input provides reliably. Complementary sensors measure different degrees of freedom, competitive sensors provide redundant estimates, and cooperative sensors derive information from their combined observations.

The measurements may differ in coordinate system, rate, latency, accuracy, and noise. Fusion therefore requires calibration and temporal alignment as well as a rule or statistical filter for reconciling the evidence.

A Bayesian fusion model treats the quantity being estimated as a hidden variable and conditions each sensor likelihood on it. Conditional independence offers a simple product of evidence, while explicit dependency, ancillary clues, and false-alarm variables prevent repeated or unreliable measurements from being counted as independent support.

3820.title: Sensor Conflict
3820.heading: Sensor Conflict
3820.content:
Sensor conflict occurs when different observations support incompatible states or values. The disagreement can result from ordinary measurement uncertainty, shared hidden influences, failure, a false alarm, or an incorrect model of sensor dependence.

Bayesian fusion does not require selecting one reading immediately. A joint model assigns relative support to the competing explanations, while explicit reliability and coherence variables can prevent conflict from producing unwarranted certainty.

3823.title: Sensitive Data Inference
3823.heading: Sensitive Data Inference
3823.content:
Sensitive data inference derives protected or intimate information from fields that appear nonsensitive on their own. Correlations among behavior, location, purchases, or relationships can reveal health, political, or other sensitive characteristics without asking for them directly.

The inference matters because the harm comes from what a system can conclude and use, not only from what a [[Data Subject]] intentionally disclosed. Governance must therefore examine analytical outputs as well as raw inputs.

3826.heading: Sensing Data Stream
3826.content:
A sensing data stream is a continuous sequence of measurements emitted by sensors or mobile devices. Individual records may have a short useful lifetime, while the stream's rate and duration make storing everything before analysis impractical.

Wireless links and resource-constrained producers expose authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, loss, and synchronization problems throughout collection.

3829.title: Semilocal Ring
3829.heading: Semilocal Ring
3829.content:
A semilocal ring is a ring with finitely many [[Maximal Ideal]]s. Its [[Jacobson Radical]] is the finite intersection of those maximal ideals.

A [[Local Ring]] is the special case with one maximal ideal. Semilocality retains enough finiteness to let several local components be handled together while distinguishing their separate residue fields.

3832.title: Semiconductor Doping
3832.heading: Semiconductor Doping
3832.content:
Semiconductor doping introduces controlled impurities into a crystal to change how electrical charge moves through it. P-type material supports mobile positive holes, while N-type material supports mobile electrons.

Joining differently doped regions creates the electrical behavior needed for transistors and other devices. Precise control of impurity concentration is essential for repeatable chip production.

In a photovoltaic junction, impurities introduce allowed energy levels inside the [[Semiconductor Band Gap]]. Donor levels near the conduction band make [[N-Type Semiconductor]] material rich in mobile electrons; acceptor levels near the valence band make [[P-Type Semiconductor]] material rich in holes. The kind and amount of impurity therefore affect the conductivity of both sides of a [[P-N Junction]].

3835.title: Semiconductor Band Gap
3835.heading: Semiconductor Band Gap
3835.content: A band gap is the forbidden interval between occupied valence states and available conduction states in an [[Electron Energy Band]] picture. An electron must gain enough energy to cross it before it can contribute to conduction. The source gives silicon's gap as about 1.1 eV; its size helps determine which [[Photon Energy]] can generate carriers and which light passes without useful conversion.

3838.title: Semi-Supervised Graph Cut
3838.heading: Semi-Supervised Graph Cut
3838.content:
A semi-supervised graph cut partitions a similarity graph while using seed labels or pairwise constraints to favor particular sides of the cut. Guidance can appear as fixed terminals, modified edge weights, or penalty terms.

The graph propagates sparse supervision through neighborhoods and can follow nonlinear structure. Performance depends on graph connectivity; weak links may isolate unlabeled regions, while spurious bridges may spread guidance across true boundaries.
